START HERE — the shading rules.

Every option below uses this same system, so settle these rules first: the benchmark, the five bands, and which columns get a direction at all.

The layout choice is separate, and it is the row of three below.

This is what the page renders today, with the benchmark-relative shading already in.

Kept honest for comparison — the three options below are measured against this, not against the old absolute-cutoff version.

PICK A DIRECTION — these differ on WHO the page is for, not on decoration.

A · the manager scanning for exceptions   ·   B · the analyst working the whole table   ·   C · the reader at a distance

Each names its own trade-off underneath. Mixing is fine — e.g. A's KPI cards with B's grouped headers.

CHOSEN — shipped in StandardReport.tsx, so all five report pages pick it up at once.

Built as drawn: severity spine, magnitude bar in grey, fill on the primary column only, exception count in the bar, benchmark named in the legend.

ONE DEVIATION: the KPI sparkline and vs-last-month delta are not built. /summary carries no prior-period figure, and rather than invent a mapping to trend measures the cards show a comparison that IS derivable — how many groups sit worse than the benchmark. Say the word and I will wire the real 12-month series.

WORTH KNOWING — the spine and fill always hang on a RATE, never a count.

A count is confounded by group size: a large branch rejects more loans and slips more accounts simply for being large, so shading it against a median punishes it for its size.

The shaded COUNT columns (fresh slippage, not-paid, no-pay, rejections) still carry colour and weight but never a fill — read them with that caveat in mind.
